Equal momenta, and K = p²/2m - so the heavy gun gets **less** energy.
**Step 1 — apply conservation of momentum.** The system starts at rest:
m_bullet v_bullet = **M_gun V_gun** ✓ equal magnitudes, opposite directions.
**Step 2 — write the kinetic energy in terms of momentum.**
K = **p²/2m** ✓
**Step 3 — compare.** With p the same for both,
K ∝ **1/m** ✓
**Step 4 — conclude.** The gun is far more massive, so its kinetic energy is far
smaller: **less than K** ✓
**The ratio.**
K_gun/K_bullet = **m_bullet/M_gun** ✓ For a 10 g bullet and a 4 kg rifle this is
**1/400** - so if the bullet carries 2000 J, the gun recoils with just **5 J**.
**Why the recoil is survivable.** That 5 J is absorbed over the **shoulder**, across a
large area and over several milliseconds ✓ The bullet's 2000 J is delivered to a tiny
area almost instantaneously. Same momentum; utterly different consequences.
**A worked instance.** 10 g bullet at 600 m s⁻¹ from a 4 kg rifle:
p = 0·01 x 600 = **6 kg m s⁻¹** ✓
V_gun = 6/4 = **1·5 m s⁻¹** ✓
K_bullet = ½(0·01)(600²) = **1800 J** ✓
K_gun = ½(4)(1·5²) = **4·5 J** ✓ precisely 1/400 of it.
**Why kinetic energy is not conserved.** The **propellant** supplies it ✓ Before firing,
both energies are zero; afterwards they total 1804·5 J, all of it from the chemical
energy of the charge. Momentum, by contrast, is conserved exactly - it was zero before
and sums to zero after.
**Why momentum is conserved despite the explosion.** The forces between gun and bullet
are **internal**, equal and opposite by Newton's third law ✓ With no external horizontal
force, the total momentum cannot change.
**The design consequence.** A **heavier** gun recoils more slowly and with less energy ✓
which is why heavy machine guns are mounted on substantial tripods and why artillery
uses recoil-absorbing mechanisms rather than mass alone.
**The same physics elsewhere.** **Alpha decay**: the light alpha takes nearly all the
energy, the heavy daughter nucleus almost none ✓ **Rockets**: the exhaust is light and
fast, the rocket heavy and slower.
**The general rule.** For any system splitting from rest, the energy divides in the
**inverse** ratio of the masses ✓
**Reading the distractors.** **K** ✗ would require equal masses. **More than K** ✗
inverts the relation, and **√K** ✗ is dimensionally impossible - the square root of an
energy is not an energy ✓
∴ less than K.

Wien's law gives **λ_m T = constant**, so the temperatures are in the **inverse** ratio
of the wavelengths.
**Step 1 — state Wien's displacement law.**
λ_m T = **b = 2·898 x 10⁻³ m K** ✓
**Step 2 — see the consequence.**
T ∝ **1/λ_m** ✓
**Step 3 — form the ratio.**
T_A/T_B = λ_B/λ_A = 480/360 ✓
**Step 4 — simplify.**
= **4 : 3** ✓
**Why the hotter star peaks at a shorter wavelength.** Higher temperature means more
energetic photons ✓ The whole spectrum shifts towards the blue - which is why a heated
poker glows dull red, then orange, then white as it gets hotter.
**The actual temperatures.**
star A: T = 2·898 x 10⁻³/360 x 10⁻⁹ = **8050 K** ✓ white, like Sirius
star B: T = 2·898 x 10⁻³/480 x 10⁻⁹ = **6040 K** ✓ yellow-white, a little hotter than
the sun
and 8050/6040 = **1·33 = 4/3** ✓
**The sun, for comparison.** λ_m ≈ **500 nm**, giving T ≈ **5800 K** ✓ in the green, which
is where the eye is most sensitive - not a coincidence.
**Why this is how stellar temperatures are measured.** One cannot put a thermometer in a
star ✓ Measuring the peak wavelength, or more practically the ratio of brightnesses
through two filters, gives the surface temperature directly. This is the basis of
stellar **colour indices** and of the spectral sequence OBAFGKM.
**The companion law.** **Stefan-Boltzmann**:
E = **σT⁴** ✓ so star A, at 4/3 the temperature, radiates (4/3)⁴ = **3·16** times as much
per unit area. A modest temperature difference makes a large difference in output.
**Why "maximum energy at" and not "only at".** A black body radiates at **all**
wavelengths ✓ The peak is merely where the curve is highest; stars emit across the whole
spectrum, which is why infrared and ultraviolet astronomy are both worthwhile.
**Why stars are good black bodies.** Their dense photospheres absorb and re-emit
radiation many times before it escapes ✓ so the emergent spectrum closely follows the
Planck curve - with absorption lines superimposed by the cooler outer layers.
**The historical note.** Explaining the **shape** of this curve defeated classical
physics - the "ultraviolet catastrophe" ✓ Planck's resolution in 1900, by quantising the
oscillators' energies, began quantum theory.
**Reading the distractors.** **3 : 4** ✗ inverts the relation and makes the bluer star
the cooler - the commonest error. **81 : 256** ✗ and **256 : 81** ✗ are the fourth
powers, belonging to a question about **power** rather than temperature ✓
∴ 4 : 3.

At equal kinetic energy, r = √(2mK)/(qB) - and for the helium nucleus the mass and
charge factors **cancel**.
**Step 1 — write the radius.**
r = mv/(qB) = **p/(qB)** ✓
**Step 2 — bring in the kinetic energy.**
p = **√(2mK)** ✓
so r = **√(2mK)/(qB)** ✓
**Step 3 — form the ratio at equal K and B.**
r_p/r_He = (√m_p/q_p) ÷ (√m_He/q_He) ✓
**Step 4 — substitute.** The helium nucleus has m = **4m_p** and q = **2e** ✓
= (√1/1) ÷ (√4/2)
= 1 ÷ (2/2)
= **1** ✓
**Step 5 — conclude.** **1 : 1** ✓
**Why the cancellation is exact.** The radius goes as **√m/q** ✓ Helium-4 has four times
the mass (factor 2 under the root) and twice the charge (factor 2 below) - and these are
precisely the numbers that make the ratio unity. It is a coincidence of the nuclide, not
a general law.
**The deuteron, which shows that.** m = 2m_p, q = e:
r_d/r_p = √2 = **1·41** ✓ a larger circle, because its charge did not double with its
mass.
**A worked instance.** K = 1 MeV, B = 0·5 T:
proton: p = 2·31 x 10⁻²⁰ kg m s⁻¹, r = 2·31 x 10⁻²⁰/(1·6 x 10⁻¹⁹ x 0·5) = **0·289 m** ✓
helium: p = 4·62 x 10⁻²⁰, q = 3·2 x 10⁻¹⁹, r = **0·289 m** ✓ identical.
**Why the path is circular.** The force **qv x B** is always perpendicular to v ✓ so it
changes direction without changing speed:
qvB = mv²/r ✓ which rearranges directly to r = mv/qB.
**What does differ - the period.**
T = **2πm/(qB)** ✓ For helium, 2π(4m)/(2eB) = **twice** the proton's. The two particles
trace the same circle, but the helium nucleus takes twice as long to complete it.
**Why no work is done.** F ⊥ v, so the kinetic energy is constant ✓ A magnetic field
steers but never accelerates in the sense of speeding up - the reason a cyclotron needs
an electric field in the gap.
**Where this is used.** **Mass spectrometry** and **bubble-chamber** analysis ✓ The
curvature of a track in a known field gives p/q at once, and with the energy known, the
particle can be identified.
**The sense of the curvature.** Both are **positive**, so both curve the same way ✓ A
negatively charged particle of the same momentum would curve oppositely - which is how
antiparticles were first recognised.
**Reading the distractors.** **1 : 2** ✗ uses the charge ratio alone; **2 : 1** ✗ the
mass ratio without the square root; **1 : 4** ✗ the mass ratio itself ✓
∴ 1 : 1.

K = h²/(2mλ²), so halving λ **quadruples** K - and the extra energy is **three times**
the original.
**Step 1 — write the energy in terms of wavelength.**
λ = h/√(2mK), so
K = **h²/(2mλ²)** ✓
**Step 2 — see the dependence.**
K ∝ **1/λ²** ✓
**Step 3 — halve the wavelength.**
K′/K = (λ/λ′)² = (1/0·5)² = **4** ✓
so K′ = **4K** ✓
**Step 4 — find the extra energy.**
ΔK = 4K − K = **3K** ✓ three times the initial kinetic energy.
**Why "additional" is the key word.** The **final** energy is 4 times the initial; the
energy that must be **supplied** is the difference, **3 times** ✓ Answering "4 times" is
the intended trap and the commonest error.
**The numbers made concrete.** For an electron at λ = 1 nm:
K = (6·63 x 10⁻³⁴)²/(2 x 9·11 x 10⁻³¹ x 10⁻¹⁸) = **2·41 x 10⁻¹⁹ J = 1·51 eV** ✓
at λ = 0·5 nm: K = **6·03 eV** ✓
additional = 6·03 − 1·51 = **4·52 eV** = **3 x 1·51** ✓
**The convenient formula.**
λ = **12·27/√V Å** for an electron through V volts ✓
1 nm = 10 Å needs V = (12·27/10)² = **1·51 V** ✓ matching the figure above.
0·5 nm needs **6·03 V** ✓
**Why the square.** λ ∝ 1/p and K ∝ p² ✓ so K ∝ 1/λ². A given factor in wavelength
appears **squared** in the energy, which is why shortening the wavelength becomes
rapidly expensive.
**The consequence for electron microscopy.** To halve the wavelength - and so double the
resolution - the accelerating voltage must be **quadrupled** ✓ This is why
high-resolution instruments run at hundreds of kilovolts, and why the gains come
slowly.
**The relativistic caveat.** Above about 50 keV the simple formula errs by more than a
per cent ✓ At these few-electron-volt energies it is exact for all practical purposes.
**A check on the momentum.** p = h/λ:
at 1 nm: **6·63 x 10⁻²⁵** ✓
at 0·5 nm: **1·33 x 10⁻²⁴** ✓ exactly **doubled**, and the energy therefore quadrupled.
**Reading the distractors.** **4 times** ✗ is the **final** energy, not the increase.
**2 times** ✗ confuses the momentum factor with the energy factor, and **0·5 times** ✗
reverses the direction of the change ✓
∴ 3 times the initial kinetic energy.

Removing the **second** electron is a hydrogen-like problem with Z = 2; add the two
ionisation energies.
**Step 1 — note what is given.** The **first** ionisation energy of helium is
**24·6 eV** ✓ - the energy to remove one electron from the neutral atom.
**Step 2 — find the second.** What remains is **He⁺**, a hydrogen-like ion with Z = 2:
E = **13·6Z²** = 13·6 x 4
= **54·4 eV** ✓
**Step 3 — add them.**
total = 24·6 + 54·4
= **79 eV** ✓
**Why the second electron is so much harder to remove.** It feels the **full** nuclear
charge of +2e ✓ In the neutral atom, each electron partly **screens** the other from the
nucleus, so the effective charge is less than 2 and the first electron leaves for only
24·6 eV. Once one has gone, there is nothing left to screen.
**Why the Bohr formula works for He⁺ but not for He.** He⁺ has **one** electron ✓ so the
13·6Z²/n² formula is exact. Neutral helium has two, and their mutual repulsion defeats
any simple analytic treatment - the first ionisation energy of 24·6 eV is a
**measured** value, which is why the question supplies it.
**The screening, quantified.** If the first electron saw an effective charge Z_eff,
13·6Z_eff² = 24·6 gives Z_eff = **1·34** ✓ noticeably less than 2, the difference being
the screening by its partner.
**Why helium is chemically inert.** 24·6 eV is the **highest** first ionisation energy
of any element ✓ Its 1s shell is full, and neither losing nor gaining an electron is
energetically available - hence no chemistry at all under ordinary conditions.
**The level diagram of He⁺.**
n = 1: **−54·4 eV** ✓
n = 2: **−13·6 eV** ✓
n = 3: **−6·04 eV** ✓ Its n = 2 level coincides numerically with hydrogen's ground
state, since 13·6(4)/4 = 13·6.
**A check in context.** Hydrogen's single electron needs **13·6 eV**; helium's pair need
**79 eV** between them ✓ nearly six times as much, reflecting the doubled nuclear charge
and the second electron's complete exposure to it.
**Where this matters.** In **stellar** spectra: He⁺ lines appear only in very hot stars,
because 54·4 eV is needed to produce the ion ✓ Their presence is a temperature
diagnostic.
**Reading the distractors.** **49·2 eV** ✗ is 2 x 24·6, supposing both electrons alike -
the intended trap. **51·8 eV** ✗ and **38·2 eV** ✗ match no consistent pair of
energies ✓
∴ 79 eV.

Energy released = **(binding energy of the products) − (binding energy of the
reactants)**.
**Step 1 — write the reaction.**
²₁H + ²₁H → **⁴₂He** ✓
**Step 2 — find the binding energy of the two deuterons.**
each: 2 nucleons x 1·1 MeV = **2·2 MeV** ✓
two: **4·4 MeV** ✓
**Step 3 — find the binding energy of the helium nucleus.**
4 nucleons x 7 MeV = **28 MeV** ✓
**Step 4 — subtract.**
Q = 28 − 4·4
= **23·6 MeV** ✓
**Why the difference is released.** Binding energy is the energy that would be needed to
**pull the nucleus apart** ✓ The helium nucleus is bound 23·6 MeV more tightly than the
two deuterons were, so forming it **liberates** that much - as kinetic energy of the
products and as gamma radiation.
**Why fusion of light nuclei releases energy at all.** The binding energy per nucleon
**rises** steeply from hydrogen to iron ✓ Deuterium sits at 1·1 MeV per nucleon, helium
at 7·07 - an exceptionally tight nucleus, the famous "alpha particle peak". Moving up
that curve releases energy.
**Why fission releases energy too.** Beyond iron the curve **falls** ✓ so splitting a
heavy nucleus also moves the nucleons to more tightly bound states. Iron-56, at 8·8 MeV
per nucleon, is the turning point, and neither fusion nor fission beyond it yields
anything.
**Comparing with fission, per nucleon.** Uranium fission releases about **200 MeV** from
236 nucleons - **0·85 MeV each** ✓ This fusion releases 23·6 from 4 - **5·9 MeV each**,
about **seven times** as much. Weight for weight, fusion is far the more energetic.
**The mass defect.**
Δm = Q/c² = 23·6/931·5 = **0·0253 u** ✓ a quarter of a per cent of the mass, converted
entirely to energy. Einstein's relation is doing the bookkeeping.
**Why fusion is so hard to achieve.** The deuterons must overcome their **Coulomb
repulsion** ✓ requiring temperatures of order 10⁸ K, at which the nuclei move fast enough
for quantum tunnelling to bring them within range of the strong force.
**Where it happens naturally.** In the **sun**, through the proton-proton chain ✓ Four
protons become one helium nucleus, releasing 26·7 MeV - the source of all sunlight, and
the reason the sun has shone for 4·6 billion years.
**The reaction pursued on earth.** Mostly **D-T** rather than D-D:
²H + ³H → ⁴He + n + **17·6 MeV** ✓ which ignites at a lower temperature. It is the
reaction ITER is built to sustain.
**Reading the distractors.** **25·8** and **26·9 MeV** ✗ mishandle the deuteron binding
energy; **12·9 MeV** ✗ is roughly half the answer, as if only one deuteron were
counted ✓
∴ 23.6 MeV.

Equate **½Iω²** with **½mv²** and solve for v.
**Step 1 — find the rotational kinetic energy.**
K = ½Iω² = ½(3)(3)² ✓
= ½(3)(9)
= **13·5 J** ✓
**Step 2 — write the translational energy.**
K = ½mv² = ½(27)v² = **13·5v²** ✓
**Step 3 — equate and solve.**
13·5v² = 13·5
v² = 1
**v = 1 m s⁻¹** ✓
**The neat cancellation.** 27 = 3 x 9, exactly the product Iω² ✓ so the halves and the
numbers cancel and v² = 1. The figures are chosen for it.
**Why the two formulas are parallel.** Rotation mirrors translation throughout ✓
mass **m** ↔ moment of inertia **I**
velocity **v** ↔ angular velocity **ω**
momentum **mv** ↔ angular momentum **Iω**
force **F** ↔ torque **τ**
½mv² ↔ **½Iω²**
The whole of rotational dynamics is the translational equations with these
substitutions.
**What moment of inertia means.** The **rotational inertia** - how hard it is to change
the rotation ✓ It depends not only on the mass but on **where** that mass sits:
I = Σmr², so distant mass counts far more. A flywheel is heavy at the **rim** for this
reason.
**Some standard values.**
ring about its axis: **MR²** ✓
disc: **½MR²** ✓
solid sphere: **⅖MR²** ✓
rod about its centre: **ML²/12** ✓
**A concrete body with I = 3 kg m².** A disc of mass 6 kg and radius 1 m ✓ since
½(6)(1)² = 3. Rotating at 3 rad s⁻¹ - about half a turn per second.
**Why a rolling body has both energies.**
K = ½mv² + ½Iω² ✓ with v = ωR for rolling without slipping. A solid sphere rolling
downhill therefore accelerates more slowly than a sliding one, because some of the
energy goes into spin.
**The angular momentum here.**
L = Iω = 3 x 3 = **9 kg m² s⁻¹** ✓ conserved if no external torque acts - which is why a
skater spins faster on pulling in her arms, reducing I and so raising ω.
**Why the answer is a modest speed.** 13·5 J is not much energy, and 27 kg is a
substantial mass ✓ 1 m s⁻¹ is a slow walk - entirely reasonable.
**Reading the distractors.** **2 m s⁻¹** ✗ would need 54 J; **0·5 m s⁻¹** ✗ only 3·4 J;
**1·5 m s⁻¹** ✗ 30·4 J ✓ Substituting back is the quickest check.
∴ 1 ms⁻¹.

Einstein's equation makes K_max depend on the **frequency** alone.
**Step 1 — write the photoelectric equation.**
K_max = **hν − φ** ✓
**Step 2 — read off the dependence.** For a given metal, φ is fixed, so K_max depends
only on **ν** ✓
**Step 3 — conclude.** The maximum kinetic energy depends only on the **frequency** of
the incident light ✓
**Why intensity makes no difference to the energy.** Intensity means **more photons**,
not more energetic ones ✓ Each electron absorbs **one** photon and receives hν,
whatever the beam's brightness. Doubling the intensity doubles the **number** of
photoelectrons - the photocurrent - and leaves their maximum energy untouched.
**Why this defeated the wave theory.** A wave delivers energy **continuously**, so a
brighter beam should produce faster electrons ✓ Experiment says otherwise, flatly, and
that discrepancy is what forced the photon picture.
**The threshold.** Below ν₀ = **φ/h** there is **no** emission at all ✓ however intense
the light and however long one waits. A wave theory can offer no reason for such a
sharp cut-off.
**The straight-line test.** Plot K_max against ν ✓
slope = **h** ✓
intercept on the energy axis = **−φ** ✓
intercept on the frequency axis = **ν₀** ✓
Millikan did exactly this, meaning to disprove Einstein, and instead measured h to one
per cent - and won the 1923 Nobel Prize for it.
**What the stopping potential measures.**
eV₀ = **K_max** ✓ so V₀ rises **linearly** with frequency and is entirely independent of
intensity. The experiment is a direct reading of the equation.
**Why "maximum".** Electrons deeper in the metal lose energy on the way out ✓ Only those
at the very surface escape with the full hν − φ, so there is a **spread** of energies
from zero up to K_max.
**What the work function is.** The **minimum** energy to free an electron from the metal
surface ✓ Caesium 2·1 eV, sodium 2·3, zinc 4·3, platinum 6·3. Only the alkali metals
respond to visible light; the rest need ultraviolet.
**Why the angle of incidence is irrelevant.** It affects how much light is **reflected**,
hence the current, but not the energy of any individual photon ✓
**Why pressure is irrelevant.** The experiment is done in **vacuum** ✓ and in any case
the photon's energy is a property of the light, not of its surroundings.
**Reading the distractors.** **Potential** ✗ - the stopping potential is a **consequence**
of K_max, not a cause. **Incident angle** ✗ and **pressure** ✗ affect neither hν nor φ ✓
∴ frequency.

Use **K = p²/2m**.
**Step 1 — write the relation.**
K = ½mv² and p = mv, so
K = **p²/2m** ✓
**Step 2 — substitute.**
K = 6²/(2 x 4) ✓
**Step 3 — evaluate.**
= 36/8
= **4·5 J** ✓
**The check by finding the velocity first.**
v = p/m = 6/4 = **1·5 m s⁻¹** ✓
K = ½(4)(1·5)² = ½(4)(2·25) = **4·5 J** ✓ the same, by the longer route.
**Why the formula is worth knowing.** It relates the two quantities **without** the
velocity ✓ which is exactly what is needed in collision problems, in de Broglie
calculations (λ = h/√(2mK)), and whenever momentum is conserved but energy is not.
**The unit check.** A newton-second is kg m s⁻¹ ✓ so p²/2m has units
(kg m s⁻¹)²/kg = **kg m² s⁻² = J** ✓ an energy, as required.
**Why N s and kg m s⁻¹ are the same.** From F = ma, 1 N = 1 kg m s⁻² ✓ so
1 N s = 1 kg m s⁻¹. **Impulse** and **momentum** share a unit because impulse **is** the
change of momentum.
**The companion relation.**
p = **√(2mK)** ✓ the same equation inverted, and the one used when the energy is given
and the momentum wanted.
**Why heavier bodies have less energy at equal momentum.** K ∝ **1/m** ✓ A 400 kg mass
with the same 6 N s carries only 0·045 J - a hundredth of this. This is why a recoiling
gun is far less dangerous than its bullet, and why the heavy daughter nucleus in alpha
decay takes almost none of the energy.
**The derivative that connects them.**
dK/dp = **p/m = v** ✓ a neat result: the rate of change of kinetic energy with momentum
is the velocity itself.
**Where this appears in relativity.** The exact relation is
E² = **p²c² + m²c⁴** ✓ which reduces to K ≈ p²/2m when p ≪ mc, and to E = pc for a
massless photon.
**A sense of the scale.** 4·5 J is the energy of a 1 kg book dropped from **45 cm** ✓ and
the body here moves at a slow walking pace.
**Reading the distractors.** **2·5 J**, **3·5 J** and **5·5 J** ✗ correspond to momenta
of 4·5, 5·3 and 6·6 N s ✓ Computing v = p/m and then ½mv² checks the answer in two
lines.
∴ 4.5 J.
